title: Measles outbreak in Wisconsin: How Pecatonica School District is protecting students
text: BLANCHARDVILLE, Wis. (WKOW) — Measles is spreading in Wisconsin, with 92 confirmed cases and six probable cases in the southwestern part of the state. Most of the cases are in Iowa and Lafayette counties. The Pecatonica School District, which serves both counties, starts classes Tuesday. District officials estimate a 97% to 98% student vaccination rate, which is above Iowa County's 86% average and well above Lafayette County's 76% average. The latest numbers show 52 confirmed measles cases in Iowa County and 37 in Lafayette County. "We've been in almost constant communication with our local health department, so getting updates from them three or four times a week," said Dr. Dani Scott, superintendent of the Pecatonica Area School District. Teachers are receiving training on symptoms to look out for, including high fever, cough and runny nose. District leaders are advising parents to use common sense. "Just kind of using some common sense and if your child is sick, keep them home," Scott said. If a child were to get sick, the district would notify other parents in the classroom. However, the decision to exempt unvaccinated students from class is left to local health departments. "If we suspect a possible case, we will reach out to our county health departments right away and then follow the necessary steps that they tell us we need to do," Scott said. District leaders say they learned from the COVID-19 pandemic and feel more prepared to handle the situation. "We're feeling more confident in our ability to respond positively and quickly ... if anything like that were to occur," Scott said.

title: Ryan Garry LLC Announces Minnesota Criminal Defense Attorney Secures Suppression of Evidence and Dismissal of Drug Charges
text: Minneapolis, Minnesota - August 31, 2026 - PRESSADVANTAGE - Minnesota criminal defense attorney Ryan P. Garry has secured the dismissal of all felony drug charges against a client after successfully challenging the expansion of a traffic stop and subsequent K9 search in Mille Lacs County District Court, Minnesota. The main witness testified that he withheld information from the police reports, hiding it from the prosecution, the court, and, most importantly, the defense attorney. In an order filed July 29, 2026, the District Court Judge Mark J. Herzing granted the defense motion to suppress the drugs and paraphernalia seized from the client's vehicle and dismissed all charges, resulting in a complete acquittal for Ryan's client. The client was facing an extensive prison sentence if convicted, and Ryan's challenge to the search of her vehicle showed the arresting officers' conduct was illegal. The ruling followed an April 9, 2026, contested hearing during which Attorney Ryan Garry challenged whether law enforcement had sufficient reasonable, articulable suspicion to transform a traffic stop into a drug investigation and K9 search. Two police officers testified at the hearing. The case began when officers stopped the client after observing the vehicle traveling 76 mph in a 45-mph zone. The defense initially did not challenge the officers' authority to make the initial traffic stop, but that changed during the hearing. Ryan's main challenge focused on what occurred after officers questioned the driver and checked the client's driving record. According to the court's findings, officers continued questioning the client about matters including travel plans, luggage, the use of a rental vehicle, and the presence of three cell phones. The client declined the officers' request to search the vehicle. An officer subsequently conducted a K9 sniff around the vehicle. After the dog alerted, officers searched the vehicle and discovered drugs that became the basis for multiple felony controlled-substance charges. Judge Herzing concluded that officers illegally expanded the stop after completing the legitimate investigation associated with the speeding violation and did so without the required reasonable, articulable, objective suspicion of criminal activity. A significant issue developed during the contested hearing concerning information that had not appeared in the arresting officer's original police report. The officer testified that, before the traffic stop, he had received information from an unidentified Brainerd-area officer indicating that the client had allegedly been observed at a known drug house. According to the court's order, this information was not included in any report and was not revealed to the prosecutor until witness preparation the day before the hearing. The court described the officer's testimony concerning the alleged drug house information as inherently incredible based on the surrounding circumstances. The work of Ryan Garry - MN Drug Crimes Attorney underscored the value of aggressive cross-examination and careful examination of police reports, body-camera footage, and other evidence. "This case reveals that some police officers hide information about their investigation to make the government's case stronger, and that unethical and sloppy law enforcement work cannot stand in this country, and defense attorneys need to be aggressive and diligent in representing their clients to reveal this very disturbing and unethical behavior," Garry said. Because the K9 sniff and resulting search flowed from an unlawful expansion of the stop, the court ruled that the drugs and paraphernalia had been unlawfully obtained and must be suppressed, resulting in a dismissal of all drug charges. Without that evidence, the court dismissed all controlled-substance charges and directed that the case file be dismissed and closed. The decision illustrates that a lawful traffic stop does not automatically grant law enforcement unlimited authority to investigate unrelated criminal activity. The outcome reflects the practice of Ryan Garry - Criminal Defense Attorney , which emphasizes constitutional challenges, motion practice, and trial preparation in cases where a client's freedom and future are at stake. "We've been in almost constant communication with our local health department, so getting updates from them three or four times a week," said Dr. Dani Scott, superintendent of the Pecatonica Area School District. Teachers are receiving training on symptoms to look out for, including high fever, cough and runny nose. District leaders are advising parents to use common sense. "Just kind of using some common sense and if your child is sick, keep them home," Scott said. If a child were to get sick, the district would notify other parents in the classroom. However, the decision to exempt unvaccinated students from class is left to local health departments. "If we suspect a possible case, we will reach out to our county health departments right away and then follow the necessary steps that they tell us we need to do," Scott said. District leaders say they learned from the COVID-19 pandemic and feel more prepared to handle the situation. "We're feeling more confident in our ability to respond positively and quickly ... if anything like that were to occur," Scott said.

title: Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany swims to safety after plane crashes in lake - The Badger Herald
text: Upgrades outlined in Mayor’s proposed Capital Budget and Improvement Plan Dane County reveals AI chatbot in non-emergency phone line WUD Wellness Committee event promotes mental health, wellbeing education amidst semester start Republican gubernatorial candidate and Rep. Tom Tiffany and his pilot swam to safety after an emergency landing in Lake Wausau night of Sept. 12, according to a statement from Marathon County Sheriff’s office. The small aircraft officially experienced engine issues before the pilot, Leonard E. Boltz, made the emergency landing, according to the preliminary accident report . The two called emergency services after landing at 8:49 p.m. before swimming to a more shallow area, according to the statement. First responders then reached them by boat and rescued them at 9:05 p.m., according to the statement. Once off the water, they were transported to the Aspirus Wausau Hospital, according to a post Tiffany made on X after he was discharged from the hospital Saturday night. Both Tiffany and Boltz sustained only minor injuries, according to the post . “I want to express my deepest gratitude to the pilot, the Wausau Fire Department, and all of the first responders who came to our aid so quickly,” Tiffany said in the post. The Marathon County Sheriff’s office also notified the Federal Aviation Administration and National Safety Board, who will look into the accident, according to the statement.

title: AI use in Wisconsin District 3 campaign ads draws criticism - The Badger Herald
text: The race to represent Wisconsin’s District 3 has turned into a debate over whether or not politicians should be allowed to campaign using artificial intelligence in advertisements, according to Wisconsin Public Radio . Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, posted an AI-generated video of Democratic nominee for District 3 Rebecca Cooke Aug. 13 to X (formerly Twitter). “I am the Anointed One. You will comply and you will vote for me. That is an order from your D.C. masters,” the video simulated Cooke saying. Van Orden used Grok, the AI companion feature that is built into X, according to WPR, and has now posted several AI generated videos to X. He said that the videos are intended to be satire, according to WPR. The use of AI creates hesitancy in politics, campaigns and with politicians, according to University of Wisconsin School of Journalism and Mass Communication Professor Young Mie Kim . “AI increases uncertainty in voters toward politics, campaigns and politicians,” Kim said. More than half of people within the United States are able to detect when AI is being used in creating images, according to a Microsoft survey. As AI increases its abilities to blend in with generic images, it will become increasingly difficult for people to identify key features that are used today to detect AI, according to Stanford University . “It’s difficult because we can’t just blame voters for not realizing the AI being used as more [political] campaigns adopt it,” Kim said. “AI can be persuasive to voters or in general, but we still don’t know its full effect. A lot of the research done is on a small scale.” Wisconsin state law requires campaign advertisements to disclose if they are using AI, but the requirement does not apply to social media posts, according to Wisconsin Act 123 passed in 2024. The bipartisan law made Wisconsin one of 31 states to enact legislation regarding the disclosure of AI in political advertisements, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures . “I think this sort of mudslinging is the opposite of what people are looking for in their members of Congress,” Cooke said in an interview with News 8 Now. The race in Wisconsin’s District 3 is one of the main targets for the Democratic Party in an effort to flip the majority control of the U.S. House, according to WPR. The use of AI has become another way politicians can market themselves on various platforms, according to UW College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence Assistant Professor Jacob Thebault-Spieker . “We’ve always had attack ads in politics, the difference now is the speed and quantity of the content being produced,” Thebault-Spieker said. Van Orden said the posts are meant to expose what he believes to be true about Cooke, and the reason Cooke is bringing the situation up is because the advertisements have been very effective, according to News 8 Now. AI is an additional tool politicians can utilize to help bolster their social media campaign presence, according to Thebault-Spieker. Politicians try to use these AI tools to try and stay relevant to general voters, according to Thebault-Spieker. “AI has been used in political campaigning before, but not on the scale we see it used today,” Kim said. Today, around 87% of strategists and campaigners use AI to help generate creative graphics, texts and visualizations for advertisements, according to the New York Times . “It’s hard to say what the right way to use AI is — some people find value in using AI while others don’t,” Thebault-Spieker said. “Depending on the tool being used and the demographic of the audience, AI can be extremely easy or extremely difficult to spot.” Van Orden’s campaign said that the video features a disclaimer about the use of generative AI directly below it, according to WPR. Democratic politicians, such as Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., have started advocating for regulations on the use of AI in campaign advertisements, according to a press release from Klobuchar’s website. The Federal Elections Committee has declined to issue new rules in regards to the use of AI in political campaigns, according to the C ampaign, Mail and Data Center. The use of AI as a tool to assist political campaigns comes as research shows the overall ineffectiveness of political ads as a whole, according to Kim. “Political ads don’t play a huge role in which candidate a voter will choose, usually, they have already made their mind up,” Kim said. The type of ad, whether positive or an attack ad, has little effect on voters and, in turn, little effect on a politician’s favorability rating, according to YaleNews. The ads generally only moved .05 of a point on the survey’s five point scale in the candidate’s favor, according to YaleNews . Political campaigns should be more careful about tailoring their advertisements to specific audiences because evidence shows that the ads’ persuasive effects deviate little from person to person or commercial to commercial, according to YaleNews. “Human-generated messages and AI-generated messages can be as persuasive as one another, but these campaigns have very little importance in terms of converting people to one side or another,” Kim said.
